newsitem.title: MEXICO: Avantel wins court order against connection fees.
newsitem.headline: Avantel wins court order against connection fees.

text.p: Mexico-based telephone company Avantel SA said on Monday that a Mexican court has ruled in its favour in a complaint it made about interconnection charges with rival Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex).

Avantel said in a statement that a district court judge suspended the interconnection charges, meaning that for the interim it will not have to pay its share of the charge, which totals roughly $422 million for all of Telmex's competitors.
The company said it was the first of this type of process that has been brought to a conclusion.
"Due to the suspension and until the said process is done, Avantel will not have to pay for any of the costs associated with the resolution," it said.
The company added that the judge's decision meant that Telmex and another company, Telnor, cannot interrupt the interconnections that Avantel already has in place.
The regulation that Avantel was fighting against was given out by the Federal Commission of Telecommunications (Cofetel).
That regulation came into effect on June 3 this year.
Avantel S.A. is a joint venture between MCI Communications and Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival, Mexico's largest banking group.
